title: LearnFlow: A K12 Gamified Adaptive Learning Platform and Reproducibility Artifact for Difficulty Measurement, Calibration and Governance Research
description:
LearnFlow is a K12 gamified adaptive-learning platform released primarily as a reproducible research artifact for the study of difficulty in adaptive learning.

Four connected lines of work are supported by this artifact:

  1. Measurement — commensurability of difficulty sources defined on different scales; drift of linear min-max fusion versus an empirical-CDF-to-logit quantile metric under monotone reparameterisation.
  2. Target — external validity of the 80-85% success-rate rule on real learner logs (assist09).
  3. Decision — ordered difficulty sequencing under a cold start, and the reliability boundary of LLM-based difficulty annotation.
  4. Governance — an intervention ledger and a seven-tuple audit schema for coexisting gamification mechanisms.

Mechanism accounting. The headline mechanism count is always reported as a triple — registered 54 / runtime effect producers 2 (at the sealed audit tag audit-m2-20260911; 14 declared mechanisms under the Route A opt-in (a declarative candidate set, not counted as AST producers), off by default) / maturity complete 9, partial 37, placeholder 8 — so that the registered figure is never read as "54 mechanisms are running". Per review 5.4, the Route A A2/A3/A4 outputs are not accepted as results. Reproduce with learnflow-backend/scripts/verify_counts.py.

Auxiliary, unvalidated module. The repository also contains a behavioural-log plus self-report measurement layer (a five-dimension learning-addiction index, LAI). It has no user data, its self-report items are purpose-built and have not undergone psychometric validation, and it is not used or validated in any of the four lines of work above. It is retained for engineering completeness only.

Reproducibility. Every headline count in the documentation is recomputed from source by scripts under learnflow-backend/scripts/; the consistency check fails loudly when a documented number diverges from the code.
